g.text: Default language of apps not yet made.
spec.lang, set per app. No other setting
Looks a key up in the selected language, then
English, then the default value, then empty.
A raw key is never shown. Plurals use
Numbers group the Indian way with Latin
One JSON file per language, loaded on demand.
English is bundled, so the fallback always
exists. Keys are typed from the English file.
Noto Sans for the eight Indic scripts, four
weights each, loaded only for the scripts in
use. A generated app takes the font of its
Length and truncation count graphemes, so
Hindi and Tamil are never cut in half.
Right-to-left is prepared but not enabled:
all ten languages run left to right.
Translating the labels of one app
The translate service asks the device first only when the on-device model can read and
write both languages (English only today). Otherwise Firebase cloud, with at most one
cloud fallback. Offline, only saved translations are used.
The result is display only: the canonical spec is never edited. Translations live in a
per-app cache and the person can review and correct them.
Internationalisation: ten languages, five independent settings
Source: src/i18n (languages, language-prefs, translator, catalogue, fonts, plural, graphemes), src/core/tasks/translate-service.ts, docs/10
